BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF ACTION AND ITS PURPOSE - continued
Initially, a small base camp may be necessary near the first drill site; later, there will be a need for a camp to support up to 50 people for a period of five months.
PART III
SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT AND ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS
No impacts of great magnitude or significance are anticipated. Those which do occur will be short-term and extremely localized such as those associated with the field camp. Such impacts will be monitored through the RISP operations. Solid and liquid wastes will be removed from the site, or disposed of on-site by proven and accepted techniques which have been employed in both the Arctic and Antarctic.
During drilling into the sea bottom, there is the remote possibility of encountering an oil deposit under pressure. Planned preventive measures should render the uncontrolled release of hydrocarbons very unlikely. Drilling will be held to reasonable depths with concurrent examination of cores for traces of hydrocarbons.
PART IV
SUMMARY OF MAJOR ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED
The objective of the proposed research cannot be realized without occupying the site and undertaking the activities associated with the project.
Alternate solutions were considered for certain project activities but not recommended. For instance, it is possible to dispose of all waste at a considerable distance from the site, however, this is considered neither environmentally necessary nor economically feasible.
The remote possibility of penetrating an oil deposit suggests two alternatives: (1) After penetrating the ice/water interface, a geophysical (seismic) program be undertaken to obtain data on the structure of sediments in the vicinity. This would remove one of the unknowns, the possibility of structural traps. However, the data to be obtained would be of limited value unless a program of high-magnitude were to be initiated. (2) Another alternative is not to proceed with the drilling into sediment and bedrock beneath the water column. Both alternatives are not recommended since the proposed project plans include careful monitoring and safety measures should significant signs of hydrocarbons be encountered.
